'''Frederick Williams Cummings''' (November 21, 1931 - January 31, 2019)<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Frederick Cummings Obituary (1931 - 2019) - Marin, CA - the Press-Enterprise |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/pe/obituary.aspx?n=frederick-w-cummings&pid=191508393 |website=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref> was an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and professor at the [[University of California, Riverside]]. He specialised in [[cavity quantum electrodynamics]], [[many-body theory]], [[non-linear dynamics]], and [[biophysics]]. He developed the [[Jaynes–Cummings model]], one atom interacting with a quantized electromagnetic field; as well as the extension of this to ''N'' atoms, known as the [[Tavis–Cummings model]]. 

==Life==
Frederick Williams Cummings was born in [[New Orleans]], Louisiana in 1931.
He served in the [[United States Army]] from 1950 to 1952, in the infantry in Korea.

He received his [[Bachelor of Science]] from Louisiana State University in 1955 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1962.{{cn|date=August 2023}} [[Edwin Thompson Jaynes]] was his doctoral supervisor, with whom he worked on the [[Jaynes–Cummings model|Jaynes–Cumming model]].

While finishing his thesis, Cummings worked at the [[Aeronutronic|Aeronutronic Research Labs]], Ford Motor Co. in Newport Beach, California from 1960 to 1963.

He became a professor at [[University of California, Riverside]] (UCR).  With his doctoral student Michael Tavis, he extended the Jaynes–Cummings model to the [[Tavis–Cummings model]] in 1968.

The revival probabilities predicted by Jaynes–Cumming model were first experimentally demonstrated in 1987 by [[Gerhard Rempe]], [[Herbert Walther]], and Norbert Klein.{{cn|date=October 2024}}

After thirty years at UCR Physics department, Cummings became [[emeritus professor]] in 1993. In the last twenty years his interest has turned to questions of [[biophysics]] of [[developmental biology|development]] and [[evolution]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=F. W. Cummings |year=2006 |title=On the origin of pattern and form in early Metazoans |journal=Int. J. Dev. Biol. |volume=50 |issue=2–3 |pages=193–208 |doi=10.1387/ijdb.052058fc |pmid=16479488 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cummings |first1=F.W |year=2004 |title=Model of Morphogenesis |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |volume=339 |issue=3–4 |pages=531–547 |arxiv=physics/0308030 |bibcode=2004PhyA..339..531C |doi=10.1016/j.physa.2004.04.047 |s2cid=13529760}}</ref>

Cummings died on January 31, 2019, in [[Marin County, California]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Personal life ===
In 1964, he married Kathleen Sturgis.  They had  one child.<ref name=":0" />
